controls.reason: Materiality and meaningful alternatives or tradeoffs require architecture judgment, while a decision register cannot prove complete capture.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All recorded decisions can have fields while a material database choice is omitted or its alternatives say none. The contract passes but architecture decisions are not fully recorded.

controls.reason: Critical-journey selection and appropriate performance objectives are product judgments; populated records cannot prove completeness or relevance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed journey can have a target while an omitted payment recovery path has none. The generic contract passes but not every critical journey is covered.

controls.reason: Whether a percentile is meaningful depends on traffic distribution, journey impact, sample size, and objective context, not field type.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A plan can use p50 and call it meaningful while rare but critical latency is hidden. Percentile presence passes but the objective still relies on an unsuitable summary.

controls.reason: The control is limited to documenting frontend and backend performance budgets, which can be expressed as versioned metrics, units, thresholds, and scopes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing side, metric, unit, threshold, or version binding fails; budget adequacy is evaluated separately.

controls.reason: Public-page inventories and performance conditions are incomplete, while finite measurements cannot prove all pages meet targets across devices, locales, networks, and states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Default pages can pass on one desktop profile while a localized page fails interaction latency on a supported phone. Fixtures pass but the public-page claim is false.

controls.reason: Endpoint or journey identifiers and latency metric, percentile, window, and threshold fields make whether targets are defined an objective record fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing target bindings or malformed metrics fail; this control does not claim the targets are achieved.

controls.reason: Instrumentation cannot prove complete database-query coverage across ORMs, replicas, jobs, dynamic SQL, and provider-side operations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed queries can report latency, count, and volume while an uninstrumented batch query dominates load. Measurements exist but database-query behavior is not fully measured.

controls.reason: Correct pool sizing is workload-dependent, and monitor configuration does not prove detection or complete pool inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every known pool can have a size and enabled dashboard while an omitted worker pool exhausts or configured alerts never fire. Fields pass but pools are not suitably sized and monitored.

controls.reason: Long-running and resource-intensive classification and suitable limits depend on workload and business semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An expensive export can be mislabeled ordinary and have no limit while all marked requests are bounded. The contract passes but a resource-intensive request remains unlimited.

controls.reason: Provider and regional inventories can omit limits, and a review record does not prove qualified review or corrective action.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed quotas can have signed reviews while a hidden account limit is unexamined. Presence passes but relevant limits were not reviewed.

controls.reason: Expected and peak cost depend on workload, pricing, allocation, growth, failure, and uncertainty assumptions whose model adequacy is not defined.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A spreadsheet can model one quiet hour as peak and omit data egress. The acceptance contract passes while operational cost is materially wrong.

controls.reason: Important outcomes and adequate SLO coverage require product and reliability judgment, and the outcome inventory can omit critical properties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All recorded SLOs can cover uptime and latency while correctness and freshness that matter to users are labeled unimportant. Records pass but important outcomes lack SLOs.

controls.reason: A bounded shutdown fixture does not exhaust load-balancer timing, races, queues, protocols, and instance types.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One HTTP instance can stop new work before shutdown while a websocket worker accepts work during a race. The test passes but the system violates the rule.

controls.reason: Overlapping and missed-run behavior needs job-specific state, timing, side-effect, retry, and recovery oracles not supplied by the generic contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cleanup job can pass simple overlap tests while a payment job duplicates charges on a specific interleaving. Fixtures pass but scheduled jobs do not safely handle overlap.

controls.reason: The statement is limited to failures actually tested: approved objective thresholds and measured recovery time in authenticated results permit exact comparison.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tested failure whose measured recovery exceeds its bound fails; a bound current result within the approved objective passes without extrapolating to untested failures.

controls.reason: Boundaries, stakeholders, concerns, assumptions, and lifecycle stage require architecture interpretation; section presence does not prove correct identification.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A document can omit an affected regulator and external data boundary while every field exists. The record passes but the system context is incomplete.

controls.reason: Materiality, forces, evidence relevance, tradeoffs, consequences, ownership, and revisit triggers are semantic and governance judgments.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A material decision can be omitted or record irrelevant evidence and a nominal owner. The schema passes while the decision is not substantively recorded.

controls.reason: Intentional-violation inventories can omit deviations, and a linked migration plan does not prove feasibility or adequate scope.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An architecture rule violation can be relabeled accidental or omitted, while listed violations link to placeholder plans. Records pass but intentional violations remain undocumented.

controls.reason: Supersession and adequate rationale require accountable architecture judgment, although immutable history itself is bounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A still-valid decision can be retired by mistake with rationale changed, or a superseded one left active. History is preserved but the rule's substantive retirement is wrong.

controls.reason: Module inventory, clear purpose, accountable ownership, adequate public contract, and prohibited dependencies require semantic architecture review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed modules can have vague purpose and nominal owner while an unlisted module exposes internals. Fields pass but modular boundaries are not clear.

controls.reason: Preconditions, outputs, invariants, side effects, errors, timing, and security properties form a large behavioral universe not exhausted by selected fixtures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A replacement can pass normal contract cases while weakening authorization on a rare error path. Tests pass but a required security property is not preserved.

controls.reason: Accepted input and promised output domains can be large or unbounded, and the proposal defines no exhaustive behavioral oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A substitute can accept all listed fixtures but reject one valid Unicode input or drop an output field in an untested state. Contract tests pass but substitutability is weakened.

controls.reason: Injected dependency identities, ownership semantics, creation scope, and lifetime are explicit binding metadata that can be required at every declared injection point.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dependency with missing, conflicting, or implicit owner or lifetime fails the versioned injection contract; no runtime quality claim is inferred.

controls.reason: A test suite cannot prove complete contract conformance across all inputs, states, errors, concurrency, and substitute implementations without an exhaustive model.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each implementation can pass examples while one substitute fails on a valid boundary input. The suite passes but conformance is incomplete.

controls.reason: Whether duplication or complexity is intentional and safer after tradeoffs is an architecture-quality judgment not proved by a note.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record can justify copied authentication logic as simpler while it creates divergent security behavior. Documentation exists but the tradeoff is not safer.

controls.reason: Supported contexts, assumptions, constraints, ownership, and service levels require product and platform judgment, not only record fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A reusable library can list all contexts and an owner while omitting a known unsupported runtime. The definition record passes but the asset's scope is inaccurate.

controls.reason: Configuration combinations can be combinatorial or dynamic, and the proposal supplies no exhaustive generator or valid-combination oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All pairwise fixtures can pass while a three-option combination is invalid and permitted. Tests pass but untested invalid configuration remains possible.

controls.reason: Reusable-asset version identity and published compatibility, deprecation, and migration policy artifacts are exact release metadata requirements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unversioned asset or missing, unpublished, or unbound policy fails; policy quality is evaluated separately.

controls.reason: Example, integration-test, and failure-semantics artifact presence does not prove representative examples, adequate tests, or complete failure meaning.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A library can provide a trivial hello-world example and one smoke test while omitting timeout failure semantics. Records pass but consumers lack required guidance.

controls.reason: A consumer registry cannot prove all runtime, transitive, copied, or externally managed consumers are tracked.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed consumer can be current while a forked service outside the registry depends on the asset. Records pass but breaking changes cannot be fully coordinated.

controls.reason: Documented interfaces and an export file do not prove teams can actually migrate state, behavior, and dependencies away from the shared asset.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A sample export can exist but lose identities and relationships required by consumers. Documentation passes while teams remain locked in.

controls.reason: Correct classification of domain, session, presentation, configuration, cache, derived, and workflow state depends on system semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A durable business fact can be labeled cache and pass enum validation. Categories exist but state is not actually distinguished.

controls.reason: Field presence does not prove complete state schema, invariants, transitions, actors, guards, side effects, and terminal states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A workflow model can omit a cancellation transition and still populate every category. The record passes but the state contract is incomplete.

controls.reason: The universe of facts and correct authority or derivation relationships is not bounded by a declared register.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered facts can name one source while another service independently mutates the same fact outside the registry. Records pass but authority is duplicated.

controls.reason: Applicable consistency, durability, freshness, ordering, and conflict requirements depend on state semantics and complete state inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed state can have fields while a replicated balance omits ordering requirements. The contract passes but per-state requirements are incomplete.

controls.reason: Applicable lifecycle behavior and adequate definitions for eight state operations require architecture meaning and complete state coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cached session can omit reset behavior or use default for each field. Schema presence passes while lifecycle behavior remains undefined.

controls.reason: Transaction and state inventories may omit platform defaults, and choosing required consistency or isolation is an architecture judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known databases can record isolation while an unlisted queue relies on default ordering. Fields pass but required semantics are still implicit.

controls.reason: Retry contexts, effects, concurrency, crashes, and duplicate paths are not exhaustively bounded by a generic execution contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Sequential retries can pass while concurrent redelivery produces two charges. Tests pass but the operation is neither idempotent nor reliably deduplicated.

controls.reason: Ordering and conflict-resolution requirements depend on domain meaning and complete asynchronous update inventories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A last-write-wins rule can be documented for balances while losing money, or an update type is omitted. The record passes but behavior is not correctly defined.

controls.reason: Concurrency primitives can be created dynamically or hidden in libraries, so selected bounds do not prove all queues, locks, pools, and parallelism are bounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured pools can have limits while an unbounded in-memory queue or goroutine fan-out is omitted. Checks pass but resource growth remains unbounded.

controls.reason: Concurrent work graphs, nested calls, races, and failure paths are not exhaustively observable through selected cancellation and backpressure tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Normal requests can propagate cancellation while a retry worker ignores deadlines and fills a queue. Fixtures pass but propagation is incomplete.

controls.reason: Dependency inventory may be incomplete and suitable timeout, retry, jitter, breaker, and fallback policy depends on failure semantics.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed dependencies can have fields while a dynamic call is omitted or retries a non-idempotent action. Records pass but per-dependency resilience is unsafe.

controls.reason: Message delivery, ordering, partitioning, retention, replay, and deduplication semantics require domain-specific decisions and complete channel inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A topic can state at-least-once without defining deduplication identity, or an unlisted queue lacks retention. Fields pass but semantics are incomplete.

controls.reason: Duplicate-delivery possibilities, consumer effects, concurrency, and crash points are not exhausted by selected execution fixtures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A consumer can deduplicate sequential duplicates while a crash after side effect before acknowledgement repeats the effect. Tests pass but idempotency fails.

controls.reason: Event immutability and schema compatibility span producers, stores, replays, consumers, and version combinations not fully bounded by examples.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known versions can interoperate while an old consumer misreads a newly optional field or a repair job mutates stored facts. Tests pass but event properties fail.

controls.reason: Queue inventories may omit channels, and adequate overload, dead-letter, poison, and replay behavior requires operational and domain judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared queues can have limits while an unlisted retry queue grows without bound, or poison behavior loses data. Records pass but queue safety is incomplete.

controls.reason: Causality and correlation across distributed calls, retries, queues, clocks, and dropped telemetry cannot be proven by a finite trace fixture.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One journey can have complete trace IDs while a retry loses parent context or timestamp ordering implies false causality. Tests pass but observability is not reliable.

controls.reason: Ownership, intended consumers, trust, availability, latency, consistency, and support expectations require accountable service-design decisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Fields can name nominal owners and arbitrary expectations while omitting a real consumer. The contract passes but the service boundary is not correctly defined.

controls.reason: Requests, responses, events, errors, and compatibility rules are a finite contract artifact set whose explicit schema presence and version binding are objective.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing or implicit schema classes, dangling references, and incompatible schema versions fail; behavioral adequacy is assessed separately.

controls.reason: Authentication, tenant, privacy, and data-classification requirements need security, privacy, and domain interpretation; field presence is insufficient.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A contract can say authorized only while omitting tenant isolation and regulated-data restrictions. Sections exist but requirements are not substantively part of the contract.

controls.reason: Correct pagination, filtering, concurrency, idempotency, rate, quota, and bulk semantics depend on API and business behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every heading can exist while pagination omits stable ordering or bulk error behavior. The record passes but semantics are incomplete.

controls.reason: Classifying every failure consistently as retryable, terminal, conflict, validation, authorization, or dependency error requires semantic judgment and complete error inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An authorization failure can be mislabeled validation or an unlisted error use a different code. Taxonomy fields pass but error semantics are inconsistent.

controls.reason: Deprecation, discovery, change-notification, migration, and retirement policy sections with versioned triggers and actions are exact lifecycle-definition artifacts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing or unbound lifecycle stages fail; actual execution of the policy is tested elsewhere.

controls.reason: External-call and journey inventories can omit calls, and trace fields do not prove correct business attribution across asynchronous work.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed HTTP calls can have trace IDs while a queue consumer's provider call loses user context. Records pass but external calls are not fully attributable.

controls.reason: Technical-debt inventories may omit obligations, while cause, consequence, interest, ownership, and remediation triggers require architecture judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed debt items can have fields while known debt is relabeled design, or interest says low without evidence. Records pass but debt is not truthfully tracked.

controls.reason: The five measures lack defined populations, clocks, attribution, units, and oracles; coordination cost and operational burden are partly judgmental.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dashboard can populate arbitrary counts for each metric while excluding cross-team delays and incidents. Fields pass but change cost is not meaningfully measured.

controls.reason: Critical invariant selection and whether automated checks prove each invariant require architecture judgment and complete executable oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A lint rule can be linked to a data-integrity invariant while testing only naming. The check runs and passes but the critical invariant is unverified.

controls.reason: Consumer migration records cannot prove every runtime, copied, external, or dormant consumer has migrated before removing a compatibility layer.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every registered consumer can be migrated while an untracked batch still needs the layer. The checker passes but removal breaks a consumer.

controls.reason: Migration-pattern classification, reconciliation completeness, and adequate exit criteria require domain and data judgment beyond a passing fixture.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Dual-write can reconcile sample rows and meet weak exit fields while rare mismatches remain. Tests pass but the pattern is used without sufficient reconciliation.

controls.reason: Supported environments, clients, protocols, formats, versions, locales, and partners are intended policy dimensions that can be explicitly enumerated in a versioned support record.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing dimensions, malformed values, or conflicting support states fail; choosing the policy is an accountable input, not a checker inference.

controls.reason: Proprietary-dependency inventories can omit dependencies, and whether stated value justifies lock-in is an architecture and business judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed vendors can have rationale useful while an embedded proprietary SDK is omitted or provides little value. Records pass but intentional dependency justification is incomplete.

controls.reason: Compatibility applicability and behavioral or operational definitions depend on consumer contracts and deployment context.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A library can mark binary compatibility not applicable despite native consumers, or define behavior vaguely. Fields pass but compatibility is not correctly defined.

controls.reason: Mixed-version and rolling-upgrade combinations, traffic, data, failures, and duration are not exhaustively specified by a generic test contract.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One old/new pair can pass a smoke test while reverse order or failover corrupts data. Tests pass but coexistence is unsafe.

controls.reason: Resumability, observability, reversal, safe roll-forward, and reconciliation need complete interruption points and data-state oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration can resume after one simulated stop while a later crash duplicates rows or reconciliation misses them. Fixtures pass but the tooling is not safely resumable and reconcilable.

controls.reason: Platform and protocol identifiers plus authoritative end-of-support dates are exact versioned record facts with freshness checks.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, stale, or conflicting dates fail; a current issuer-bound date passes without judging migration priority.

controls.reason: Field presence does not prove transparent or defensible measurement boundaries, allocation, data sources, and uncertainty treatment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report can hide exclusions in vague boundary text and set uncertainty zero while all fields exist. The record passes but measurement is not transparent.

controls.reason: A signed review and published metrics do not prove regressions were interpreted correctly or progress is genuinely auditable against sound baselines.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team can omit a regression from the report or use a changed baseline while every artifact is published. Records pass but progress is not auditable.
